The user wants uninstaller strings for a desktop app in English. They want JSON output only. Let me craft:

s1: title of dialog asking whether to uninstall — e.g., "Uninstall MyApp?" or "Uninstall Application"
s2: button performing uninstall — "Uninstall"
s3: button keeping the app — "Cancel" or "Keep App"
s4: status line while files being removed — "Removing files…" or "Uninstalling… Please wait."
s5: error when app still running — "Uninstall failed because [App] is still running. Please close MyApp and try again." Should be generic without app name? Could use a placeholder, but better to write self-contained. Since no app name given, I could use "the application" or include a placeholder like {app}. The user said "strings" — placeholders are common in localization. But safer to keep generic: "The application could not be uninstalled because it is still running. Please close the application and try again."

Maybe use a generic name. I'll go with placeholders? The instruction says English strings for a desktop app's uninstaller. I'll write generic without placeholders to be safe, or use {AppName}? Many localization tasks accept placeholders. But without knowing, generic is safer.

Return only JSON.{"s1":"Uninstall this application?","s2":"Uninstall","s3":"Cancel","s4":"Removing files… Please wait.","s5":"Uninstall failed because the application is still running. Please close the application and click Uninstall again."}

parsed.s5: Uninstall failed because the application is still running. Please close the application and click Uninstall again.
